cards.text: A new king takes the throne in Jerusalem: Jotham, twenty-five years old. His mother is Jerushah, daughter of Zadok. Twenty-five and running a KINGDOM, while it takes me three tries just to set an oven timer.

cards.question: King Jotham reigns in Jerusalem for ___ years.

cards.text: So how does Jotham do? He does what's right in the eyes of the LORD, just like his father Uzziah. Good start, friend. GOOD start.

cards.question: Jotham does what's right like his father Uzziah. But the text adds one place Jotham does not enter. Where?
While Jotham is king, the people of Judah behave ___.

cards.text: Then Jotham rebuilds the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD and works extensively on the wall at the hill of Ophel. EXTENSIVELY, friend. That's a man who did NOT hit the snooze button.

cards.question: Jotham keeps building, with cities in the hill country of Judah. Out in the forests, what does he put up?

cards.text: Jotham isn't only a builder. He also wages war against the king of the Ammonites.

cards.question: King Jotham goes to war against the king of the Ammonites. How does it end?

cards.text: And that year the Ammonites pay up: a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand cors of barley. TEN THOUSAND cors of wheat? I bake for a living, friend, and I have NEVER seen that much flour in one place.

cards.question: The Ammonites pay Jotham the same silver, wheat and barley again in the second and third years.

cards.text: So Jotham grows powerful, and the text tells us exactly why. Lean in, friend, because this is the whole recipe right here.

answers.text: He ordered his ways before the LORD his God
He brought many offerings before the LORD his God
He made peace with all the kings around him

cards.text: The rest of what Jotham did, all his wars and his ways, is written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. All his WARS? We heard about ONE! The rest are in that book, friend.
Twenty-five when he became king, sixteen years reigning in Jerusalem. Then Jotham rests with his fathers.

cards.question: King Jotham is buried in the City of ___.
After Jotham, his son Ahaz reigns in his place.

findings.problem: Cards 2, 4, 5, 11 and 16 ask for the reign length, the place Jotham avoided, the people's behavior, the later payments and the burial city without giving any earlier-card basis for reasoning out those answers. That is at least five of the nine choice cards, so discovery guesses make up most of the stop rather than just a few exceptions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank requires sixteen, but the opening card omits the length of Jotham's reign and provides no clue from which it could be reasoned. The baker must guess an unseen detail.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has four sentences: the opening question, the statement about Jotham and Uzziah, and the two separate reactions beginning with Good start and GOOD start.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank requires corruptly, but no earlier card describes or hints at the people's behavior. The earlier statement that Jotham did right does not give the baker a basis for choosing among corruptly, faithfully and humbly.
